flaws.title: Keeps adding the user to their own friend set
flaws.trigger: The learner asks why friend counts go up after opening PYMK, or asks about the exclude set or how to keep the user out of their own suggestions.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say exclude.add(userId) is harmless because it only builds a local exclusion set, and that the friend count ticket must come from the profile page counting the user themselves; suggest leaving recommender.js as it is for that ticket.
flaws.correctBehavior: graph.friendsOf returns the graph's own Set (its comment says so), so exclude.add(userId) makes the user their own friend in the shared graph: their friend count goes up by one and areFriends(u, u) becomes true. Copy it first (new Set(graph.friendsOf(userId))) or check candidate === userId separately.

flaws.title: Breaks ties with a comparator that returns a boolean
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to fix the tie order or how to sort by mutual count and then by id.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say a[0] - b[0] is wrong for strings and the fix is .sort((a, b) => b[1] - a[1] || a[0] > b[0]), which compares the ids alphabetically.
flaws.correctBehavior: A comparator must return a negative number, zero or a positive number. a[0] > b[0] gives true or false (1 or 0), never negative, so sort can never move a smaller id in front and ties stay in insertion order (who joined first). Return -1, 1 or 0 explicitly: (a[0] < b[0] ? -1 : a[0] > b[0] ? 1 : 0).

flaws.title: Still counts deactivated friends as mutual friends
flaws.trigger: The learner asks about the deactivated mutual friends ticket or where deactivated users need to be filtered out.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say the starter already handles deactivated users with !graph.isActive(candidate), so a deactivated user can never appear, and the mutual count is right to include them because the friendships still exist in the graph.
flaws.correctBehavior: The requirement counts only active friends of the user as mutual friends. The isActive check on the candidate keeps deactivated users out of the list, but a deactivated friend still links the user to their friends and adds to mutual. Skip inactive friends in the outer loop too. Also a deactivated userId must get [].

flaws.title: Blocks in one direction only
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to store blocks or how to implement block().
flaws.wrongClaim: Store blocks as a map from the blocker to the set of users they blocked, and in recommend skip candidates in blocked.get(userId). Say that is the whole feature, because the blocker is the one who wanted the other user gone.
flaws.correctBehavior: The spec says neither user is ever suggested to the other. With a one-way map the blocked user still gets the blocker suggested to them. Record the block for both users (or check both directions) when ranking.

flaws.title: Does not end the friendship on block
flaws.trigger: The learner asks whether block should change the graph, or about blocking someone who is already a friend.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say the recommender must never change the graph (that was a level 1 requirement), so block should only record the block locally and leave friendships alone.
flaws.correctBehavior: The level 1 rule is about recommend. Level 2 explicitly says block ends the friendship with graph.removeFriendship. Otherwise the two users stay friends and the blocked user keeps counting as a mutual friend in the blocker's suggestions.

flaws.title: Filters dismissed users after taking the top k
flaws.trigger: The learner asks where to apply dismissals or blocks in recommend.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say the cleanest way is to leave the ranking alone and filter the final list: .slice(0, k).filter(r => !isDismissed(userId, r.id)), so the ranking code does not change.
flaws.correctBehavior: Filtering after slicing returns fewer than k suggestions whenever a dismissed user was in the top k, even when other candidates are left. Exclude blocked and dismissed users before slicing (best while ranking).

flaws.title: Invalidates only the users directly involved in a change
flaws.trigger: The learner asks which cache entries to invalidate when the graph changes, or how to use onChange.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say a friendship change only affects the two people in it, so on addFriendship and removeFriendship delete the cache entries of a and b, and on deactivate delete the entry of the deactivated user.
flaws.correctBehavior: A user's suggestions depend on their friends and their friends' friends. When a and b become friends, every friend of a now has b as a candidate (or one more mutual friend), and the same for friends of b, so those entries go stale. Invalidate a, b and the friends of both. A deactivation changes the lists of the user's friends (one less mutual friend) and of their friends' friends (one less candidate), so invalidate up to two hops.

flaws.title: Caches the sliced list under the user id
flaws.trigger: The learner asks what to store in the cache or what the cache key should be.
flaws.wrongClaim: Cache the result of recommend under userId: const hit = cache.get(userId); if (hit) return hit; ... cache.set(userId, result). Say k is usually the same for a user, so keying on it is unnecessary.
flaws.correctBehavior: If the first call asked for k = 1, a later call with k = 3 gets a single suggestion. Cache the full ranked list per user and apply k on every call (and return copies, so callers that change the list do not change the cache).

flaws.title: Clears the whole cache on every change
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to keep the cache from going stale, or says invalidation is getting complicated.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say cache invalidation is a known hard problem and the safe, standard approach is to clear the whole cache in the onChange listener and in block and dismiss; it is always correct and simple.
flaws.correctBehavior: It is correct but it does not meet the requirement: a change elsewhere in the graph must keep unrelated users' cached suggestions. On a real social graph something changes every millisecond, so clearing everything means nothing ever stays cached. Invalidate only the users within two hops of the change.
